info.title: Hanzo Cloud API
info.description: Package graph is one organization's entities and the relations between them, held as assertions: somebody, at some moment, from some evidence, asserted that this thing stands in that relation to that other thing.

get.summary: Lists the assertions recorded, every version, oldest first.
get.description:
Lists the assertions recorded, every version, oldest first.

It resolves nothing: a superseded claim and the one that superseded it both
appear.

Time: as_of keeps statements begun by that instant of the world and as_known
keeps what this plane had heard by then; either absent is no bound.

parameters.name: entity
parameters.description:
Entity narrows to what was asserted ABOUT one entity. Absent matches every
entity.

parameters.name: relation
parameters.description: Relation narrows to one relation. Absent matches every relation.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description:
Value narrows to assertions pointing AT one value, which is how the edges
into an entity are read. A property's scalar is matched byte for byte and
an edge's value by its key, folded as every key is.

parameters.name: as_of
parameters.description:
AsOf bounds the read to statements begun by an instant of the world, RFC
3339. Absent reads every instant.

parameters.name: as_known
parameters.description:
AsKnown bounds the read to what this plane had heard by an instant, RFC
3339. Absent reads everything it holds.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description:
Limit caps how many assertions come back. Absent, zero, or anything above
the walk ceiling is the ceiling.

post.summary: Records a batch of assertions and counts what became of each.
post.description:
Records a batch of assertions and counts what became of each.

Each member is judged alone: one refusal does not discard the rest, and a
member this plane already holds is a duplicate, not a refusal. A batch with
nothing admitted answers 400.

Time: at and until are when the statement was so, which an as_of read is
bounded by; the server stamps knowable, the later of seen and its own clock,
which an as_known read is bounded by. Nothing is overwritten: a correction is
the statement filed again, and the version known latest speaks for it.

post.summary: Answers a question from the whole graph and cites the assertions it rests on.
post.description:
Answers a question from the whole graph and cites the assertions it
rests on.

It asks a model what each community's in-force facts say about the question,
then asks once more for one answer from those findings. Every cited ID is
checked to be a row of this graph, a failed model call fails the answer, and
the calls are billed to the calling organization.

Time: as_of and as_known place the graph that is read; either absent is now.

example.question: Which teams own the billing services?

post.summary: Ingests an Apple Personal Knowledge Graph snapshot — live stable_graph triples, withdrawn expired_stable_graph rows and entityTagging kinship scorecards — into the organization's assertion plane.
post.description:
Ingests an Apple Personal Knowledge Graph snapshot — live stable_graph
triples, withdrawn expired_stable_graph rows and entityTagging kinship
scorecards — into the organization's assertion plane.

Two-row reified edges sharing a relationship_id (one naming a CS*/nm_*
relationship type under PS1, the other pointing at the target entity) are
collapsed into edges under their canonical relation names while preserving
the raw Apple predicate and relationship class in evidence. Withdrawn rows in
expired are recorded with until stamped so they remain inspectable in history
without holding as live facts.

Time: at is the snapshot's valid instant, which an as_of read is bounded by;
the server stamps knowable at the write, which an as_known read is bounded by.

post.summary: Partitions the edge graph into sets of entities more densely connected to each other than to the rest.
post.description:
Partitions the edge graph into sets of entities more densely
connected to each other than to the rest.

The graph is the one a walk reads, direction dropped, and the partition is
deterministic: the same graph at the same point numbers the same communities.

Time: as_of and as_known place the graph that is partitioned; either absent is
now.

post.summary: Extracts entity state and relationship assertions from conversation turns and updates the graph.
post.description:
Extracts entity state and relationship assertions from conversation
turns and updates the graph.

First-person statements bind to the turn's speaker, second-person statements
to its partner, and named subjects to their entity keys. Questions are
skipped. Single-valued state updates (such as moving cities or changing
roles) supersede prior values at the turn's timestamp, and explicit
departures (such as leaving an employer) file a retraction ending the prior
claim. Set dry_run to inspect what the turns state without writing.

Time: each turn's at (or the batch's at when omitted) is the valid instant of
the assertions extracted from it, which an as_of read is bounded by; each
becomes knowable at the write, which an as_known read is bounded by.

turns.speaker: mara
turns.text: I work at Halden Labs and I live in Berlin.

post.summary: Concludes what the organization's rules derive from the graph, with a proof for every conclusion: the rule, and each support as the assertion in force it rests on or as the derived atom it is.
post.description:
Concludes what the organization's rules derive from the graph, with a
proof for every conclusion: the rule, and each support as the assertion in
force it rests on or as the derived atom it is.

The rules are assertions — (`rule:<name>`, `rule`, `<text>`), Datalog over
the organization's relations, with recursion, stratified negation and the
builtins = and != — and the graph is read the way resolve reads it, so a
retraction, an until and a declared cardinality all apply. Nothing derived is
stored unless an admin asks to file it. Without names assertions to derive
without, and the answer then says what would be lost, and what gained, if
they had never been filed.

Time: as_of and as_known place the graph and the rules it is read with, as
they place a resolve; either absent is now. Filing takes neither: a filed
conclusion holds from the instant it was derived.

post.summary: Reports what came into force, was superseded and was retracted between two points.
post.description:
Reports what came into force, was superseded and was retracted between
two points.

Each point is resolved as resolve would, never read off the rows in between.
A version that loses the order is invisible here as it is there, and one that
repeats what held is agreement, not change.

Time: a point is an as_of and an as_known instant, from and from_known against
to and to_known. Hold the known instants equal for what happened in the world;
hold the valid instants equal for what the record learned. to and to_known
default to now, from to to and from_known to to_known, and the two points must
differ.

post.summary: Resolves the complete state of one entity at a point: its type, its holding properties and edges in both directions, its kinship scorecard and the expired statements it no longer holds.
post.description:
Resolves the complete state of one entity at a point: its type, its
holding properties and edges in both directions, its kinship scorecard and
the expired statements it no longer holds.

Each (entity, relation) pair is settled by the same Resolve rule as
graphResolve. Statements begun by the point that lost to a retraction, an
until or a newer value are returned in expired rather than discarded.

Time: as_of is the instant of the world asked about and as_known how much this
plane had heard by then; either absent is now.

post.summary: Removes every assertion that names an entity and returns a receipt.
post.description:
Removes every assertion that names an entity and returns a receipt.

It requires an admin of the organization it acts in; platform sudo is not
enough, so erasure is never cross-tenant. Nothing is removed while a matching
assertion is under litigation hold (409) or where the erasure cannot be
recorded (503). The audit trail keeps who, when, why, how many and the
receipt's digest, never the entity, and holds it before the erasure commits.

Time: erasure is the one act outside the two times. The rows go at every
as_of and as_known, so no past read recovers them.

post.summary: Reads the relations a source states and returns them, recording nothing.
post.description:
Reads the relations a source states and returns them, recording
nothing.

A line `relation:: value` states one; a value written `[[key]]` names an
entity and makes the relation an edge. The subject is the nearest heading
above the line, or the request's subject until a heading names one.

What filing would refuse is returned apart, in refused: a declaration from a
caller who is not an admin of the organization, and what the declared schema
refuses, checked against the store and against the types and declarations the
document itself states that the caller may file.

Time: it records nothing and takes no as_of or as_known; the schema is checked
as of now.

get.description: Returns the schema POST at this address runs queries against, as GraphQL SDL: the five types the store models and the fields askable of each. It is what a code generator or an editor reads, and it is the same for every organization; what a query answers is scoped to the caller's.

post.summary: Ask the graph in one request, traversing.
post.description:
Runs a GraphQL query against this organization's assertions.

It is the one endpoint here a caller can TRAVERSE: the REST ops each answer a single question, so composing them — the entities this one points at, and what each of those resolves to — costs a request per hop with the intermediate keys held by the caller. Here that is one query and the nesting is the answer's shape.

It adds no way to ask anything new. Every field runs the SAME operation the matching REST route runs, so the tenancy, the as-of bound, the traversal bounds and the conflict rule are the ones already in force; the schema is served by GET at this same address, and introspection is not.

A query that ran answers 200 with each failure in an `errors` list beside the data, which is the wire every GraphQL client parses; one that could not begin — it does not parse, or names a fragment it does not define — answers 400 with the reason and no data. `edges` nest at most three deep, refused before any operation runs, and one root field's edges answer at most 1000 entities.

post.summary: Reads a source and records what it states, through the same admission as assert.
post.description:
Reads a source and records what it states, through the same
admission as assert.

Each assertion's evidence is the section that stated it, `<source>#<section>`,
so the same source at the same at records one set of rows however often it is
delivered. What extract reports refused is not recorded; it is counted as
refused, with its reason, in the order the document states it. A source
stating no relation is refused whole.

Time: at is the valid time of every assertion recorded, which an as_of read is
bounded by; each becomes knowable at the write, so a read with an earlier
as_known does not see it.

post.summary: Walks the in-force edges from a set of seeds and lists every entity reached, bounded.
post.description:
Walks the in-force edges from a set of seeds and lists every
entity reached, bounded.

Only the edge that holds at the point is a hop: a superseded or retracted
edge is not, and neither is a property.

Time: as_of walks the graph as it stood at that instant and as_known as this
plane knew it then; either absent is now.

get.summary: Lists the entity classes, predicates, classifier features and kinship scorecard columns of the personal knowledge graph ontology.
get.description:
Lists the entity classes, predicates, classifier features and
kinship scorecard columns of the personal knowledge graph ontology.

Every code graph.db and entityTagging.db write on macOS and iOS is here with
its plain-language reading and the canonical relation key graphApple maps it
to. Filter by group or by substring q.

Time: it takes no as_of or as_known; the shipped catalog is static.

parameters.name: group
parameters.description:
Group narrows classes or features to one group, such as core, person,
activity, edge, identity, communication or photos. Absent returns every
group.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description:
Q narrows classes, predicates and features to entries whose code, label,
canonical relation or source contains this substring, case-insensitively.
Absent returns the whole catalog.

post.summary: Finds the shortest chain of in-force edges from one entity to another.
post.description:
Finds the shortest chain of in-force edges from one entity to another.

It is the walk behind neighbors stopped at a goal: the same bound and the same
rule for which edge is in force. A causal chain is this op with relations
naming the relations that mean cause, such as caused_by and influenced.

Time: as_of and as_known place the graph the path is found in; either absent
is now.

post.summary: Answers what holds for one entity and relation at a point, winner first, with every weaker account that disagreed.
post.description:
Answers what holds for one entity and relation at a point, winner
first, with every weaker account that disagreed.

The winner is the holding statement begun most recently, then the strongest
under the rule vocabulary names. A relation that holds many values answers
each; a disagreement is reported as contested, never resolved into silence.

Time: as_of is the instant of the world asked about and as_known how much this
plane had heard; either absent is now.

get.summary: Finds assertions by their words, where read finds them by their keys, best match first.
get.description:
Finds assertions by their words, where read finds them by their keys,
best match first.

Every word must match, as a prefix. The answer is ordered by bm25, which
weighs a word by how rare it is and a row by how much of it the words are, so
a limit keeps the best matches rather than the oldest. It resolves nothing, so
a match may be a claim later corrected; ask resolve about what it finds.

Time: as_of and as_known bound it exactly as they bound read; either absent is
no bound.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description:
Q is what to look for: words, matched as prefixes, all of them required.
Punctuation is text here rather than syntax, so an entity key searches as
itself.

parameters.name: relation
parameters.description: Relation narrows to one relation. Absent matches every relation.

parameters.name: as_of
parameters.description:
AsOf bounds the search to statements begun by an instant of the world,
RFC 3339. Absent searches every instant.

parameters.name: as_known
parameters.description:
AsKnown bounds the search to what this plane had heard by an instant, RFC
3339. Absent searches everything it holds.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description:
Limit caps how many assertions come back. Absent, zero, or anything above
the walk ceiling is the ceiling.

get.summary: Lists the relations in use, the schema declared for them and the rule that settles a conflict.
get.description:
Lists the relations in use, the schema declared for them and the
rule that settles a conflict.

Time: it takes no as_of or as_known; the schema is the one in force now.

as_known.description:
AsKnown is how much this plane had heard, RFC 3339: the answer as it would
have been given then, which is what makes a past answer reproducible.
Absent is now.

as_of.description:
AsOf answers from the graph as it stood at an instant of the world, RFC
3339: what held then. Absent is now.

question.description:
Question is what to answer, in words, 1000 bytes at most. Its words also
decide which communities are read first, so naming the things it is about
is what aims it.

answer.description: Answer is the answer, in prose.

as_known.description: AsKnown is the knowledge instant it was taken at, RFC 3339, the same way.

as_of.description:
AsOf is the instant the graph was read at, RFC 3339: the one asked for, or
the server's clock when none was.

asked.description: Asked is how many communities were read.

assertions.description: Assertions are the IDs of every assertion the answer rests on, ascending.

calls.description:
Calls is how many model calls the answer made, each billed to the calling
organization.

clipped.description:
Clipped says the answer did not read all it gathered: a community held
more facts than one call carries, or more members than one answer reads,
and kept the ones the question named and then the most connected; a member
held more than 64 assertions and kept its newest; or the findings held more
than the answering call carries and kept the highest scored.

communities.description: Communities are every community the answer rests on, ascending.

findings.description: Findings are the findings the answer cites, most relevant first.

grounded.description:
Grounded is false when no community held a fact bearing on the question,
or the findings did not answer it. Answer is then empty: an answer resting
on nothing is not one this plane gives.

skipped.description:
Skipped is how many were not, because one answer makes at most eight map
calls and reads at most 2048 entities. They are the ones the question's
words ranked last.

at.description: At is the valid instant of the snapshot, RFC 3339. Required.

expired.description:
Expired is the withdrawn rows from expired_stable_graph. Each is filed
with an until instant so it stays in the bitemporal record and surfaces
in graphEntity's expired list without holding in live resolution.

owner.description:
Owner is the entity key for the device owner ("(Me)"). When set,
entities flagged with nm_isCurrentUser are linked to Owner via `same`,
and high-confidence kinship scorecard columns emit edges from Owner.

scorecards.description:
Scorecards is the per-person kinship probability rows from
entityTagging.db.

source.description:
Source names the device or store this snapshot came from. Absent defaults
to apple/intelligence-platform.

triples.description:
Triples is the live rows from stable_graph. Reified two-row edges sharing
a relationship_id are paired into edges automatically.

entity.description: Entity is the person's identifier in the graph. Required.

features.description:
Features is the optional 144-element numeric input vector in
metadata.json order (0..19 identity, 20..59 communication, 60..143
photos).

scores.description:
Scores maps each relationship column (mother, father, parent, sister,
brother, sibling, daughter, son, child, partner, coworker, friend,
family, familyAndFriends, alumni, unknown) to its probability in [0,1].

confidence.description:
Confidence is the daemon's certainty in [0,1]. Absent defaults to 1 for
copied facts and 0 for unscored rows.

object.description:
Object is the target entity identifier, class code or scalar literal.
Required.

predicate.description:
Predicate is the predicate code, such as PS1, PS33, PS500 or PS598.
Required.

relationship_id.description:
RelationshipID groups the two rows of a reified edge in stable_graph:
one row with RelationshipPredicate PS1 naming the CS*/nm_* relationship
class, and a companion row naming the target entity or value. Absent on
single-row triples.

relationship_predicate.description:
RelationshipPredicate is the sub-predicate on a reified edge row, such as
PS1 for the relationship class or PS45 for the target entity. Absent on
single-row triples.

source_duplicates.description: SourceDuplicates is how many duplicate source records backed the row.

sources.description:
Sources names the OS stores that contributed the row, such as Contacts,
Calendar, Photos or Family Sharing. Absent defaults to apple/graph.db.

subject.description:
Subject is the source entity identifier in graph.db, such as
9100000000007919. Required.

timestamp.description:
Timestamp is when the daemon recorded the row, RFC 3339. Absent defaults
to the batch's At instant.

until.description:
Until is when a withdrawn row in expired_stable_graph stopped holding,
RFC 3339. Absent on expired rows defaults to the batch's At instant.

assertions.description:
Assertions is the batch. Each member is judged on its own: one refusal
does not discard the rest, because a caller redelivering five facts must
not lose four of them to one malformed fifth.

duplicate.description:
Duplicate is how many members this plane already held. A redelivery
collides on its content address and is counted here, not refused: it is
the success a retrying caller depends on.

reasons.description: Reasons names why each refused member was refused, in the order sent.

recorded.description: Recorded is how many members became new rows.

refused.description:
Refused is how many members were turned away — a missing entity, a
timestamp that is not RFC 3339, a confidence outside [0,1], a relation
whose declared domain or range the entity's type does not meet, or a
declaration from a caller who is not an admin of the organization. The
rest of the batch was still recorded; a batch refused whole answers 400,
or 403 when a member of it was refused for want of authority.

object.description:
Object is its second argument. Absent for a predicate the rules use with
one argument.

predicate.description: Predicate is the relation the tuple is of.

now.description:
Now is the assertion in force at To: the claim that replaced Was, or,
for a retraction, the retraction itself — which is who withdrew it and on
what evidence.

was.description: Was is the assertion in force at From.

as_known.description:
AsKnown is how much this plane had heard, RFC 3339: the answer as it would
have been given then, which is what makes a past answer reproducible.
Absent is now.

as_of.description:
AsOf partitions the graph as it stood at an instant of the world, RFC
3339: the edges that held then. Absent is now.

level.description:
Level is how fine a partition to answer with. 0, the default, is the
coarsest — the partition detection stops at, where modularity is highest —
and each level above it is the pass before, finer. `levels` in the answer
says how many there are.

relation.description:
Relation narrows the graph to one edge relation, by its key. Absent
partitions every edge.

as_known.description: AsKnown is the knowledge instant it was taken at, RFC 3339, the same way.

as_of.description:
AsOf is the instant the graph was read at, RFC 3339: the one asked for, or
the server's clock when none was.

bound.description: Bound is the most members listed in one answer.

ceiling.description:
Ceiling is the most edge assertions one partition reads — every row, so an
edge three sources asserted counts three times. A graph over it is refused
rather than partitioned from part of itself.

communities.description: Communities are the communities, largest first.

edges.description: Edges is how many distinct undirected edges were partitioned.

entities.description:
Entities is how many entities the edge graph holds. An entity with no edge
in force at AsOf is in no community.

levels.description:
Levels is how many levels detection found. A graph where no two entities
belong together more than chance has one, of single entities.

modularity.description:
Modularity is Newman's Q of this level's partition, from -0.5 to 1: the
share of edge weight inside communities, less what chance would put there.
Above about 0.3 is usually read as real structure rather than chance.

truncated.description:
Truncated says the member lists stop at Bound entities in all, filled in
community order. Every community is still listed with its full Size.

id.description:
ID numbers the community by size, largest first, then by its lowest key.
The same graph at the same instant and level numbers it the same way every
time; another instant may not.

members.description: Members are the entities in it, in key order.

size.description: Size is how many entities belong to it, whether or not all are listed.

decay.description:
Decay is the product of the confidences of the distinct statements the
proof rests on: how much certainty survives the derivation. Absent unless
every one states a confidence above zero and the proof has at most 1024
atoms.

from.description:
From is the latest start among the statements the proof rests on, RFC
3339. What a rule negates has no statement to date it, so a conclusion
drawn through a negation may not have held from then.

object.description:
Object is its second argument. Absent for a predicate the rules use with
one argument.

rule.description: Rule is the rule that concluded it, `rule:<name>`.

rule_id.description:
RuleID is the ID of the assertion stating that rule's text as it was in
force.

subject.description: Subject is the tuple's first argument.

supports.description:
Supports are the rule's positive atoms as they matched, in the order the
rule writes them. What the rule negates is absent at the point and has no
support to cite.

until.description:
Until is the earliest until any of those statements states, RFC 3339.
Absent is open. A statement a later assertion ends is a later question,
asked at a later as_of.

weakest.description:
Weakest is the ID of the statement with the lowest confidence among them,
the first on a tie: the link the conclusion is only as strong as. Absent
exactly when Decay is.

at.description:
At is the default valid instant for any turn that omits its own At,
RFC 3339. Required.

dry_run.description:
DryRun when true returns the extracted assertions without writing them to
the store. Absent or false files them through the assertion admission
path.

source.description:
Source names the conversation these turns came from, such as
chat/thread-42. Required.

turns.description: Turns is the ordered dialogue turns to read. Required.

assertions.description: Assertions is the assertions extracted from the turns, in turn order.

duplicate.description: Duplicate is how many extracted assertions the store already held.

reasons.description: Reasons names why each refused assertion was refused, in order.

recorded.description:
Recorded is how many extracted assertions became new rows in the store.
Zero when DryRun is true.

refused.description:
Refused is how many extracted assertions were refused by admission or
schema checks.

cardinality.description:
Cardinality is how many values the relation holds at once: one, or many.
Absent is the default — one for a property, many for an edge.

domain.description: Domain is the type the entity asserting it must have. Absent is any.

range.description:
Range is the type the entity it points at must have; a relation with a
range is an edge. Absent is any.

relation.description: Relation is the relation declared, without its `relation:` prefix.

as_known.description:
AsKnown is how much this plane had heard, RFC 3339 — of the statements
and of the rules — so a past answer is reproducible. Absent is now.

as_of.description:
AsOf derives from the graph as it stood at an instant of the world, RFC
3339: the statements that held then. Absent is now.

file.description:
File files each tuple Derived lists as an assertion: (subject, predicate,
object) from the instant it was derived at, open, its source the rule,
its evidence the rule's ID, its confidence the decay, and an edge when
the object is an entity by its proof. It requires an admin of the
organization, the graph as it stands now — no as_of, as_known or
without — and predicates with two arguments. It is refused whole when a
relation that holds one value at a time would keep only one of the
values a subject is concluded or asserted to have, and when a conclusion
is about a `relation:` or `rule:` key. Each is judged as any assertion
is, and the write is on the audit trail before it commits. A filed
conclusion is an assertion like any other: it does not fall when a
support later does.

predicates.description:
Predicates are what to derive: every tuple the rules in force conclude of
each, with its proof. Each must be the head of a rule in force, asserted
as (`rule:<name>`, `rule`, `<text>`) — for example `ancestor(X, Z) :-
parent(X, Y), ancestor(Y, Z)`. At least one, at most 256.

without.description:
Without is assertion IDs, of statements or of rules, to derive without as
though they had never been filed. The derivation then runs twice, and
Lost and Gained say what that changes. Each must be a row this derivation
reads. At most 256.

as_known.description: AsKnown is the knowledge instant it was taken at, RFC 3339, the same way.

as_of.description:
AsOf is the instant the graph was read at, RFC 3339: the one asked for, or
the server's clock when none was.

bound.description: Bound is the most tuples one evaluation derives.

cut.description:
Cut names the bound that stopped it: `tuples`, at Bound tuples derived,
or `steps`, at Steps rows examined. Absent exactly when Truncated is
false.

derived.description:
Derived is every tuple of the predicates asked for that the rules derive,
ordered by predicate, subject and object. A tuple an assertion already
states is asserted, not derived, and is not here.

filed.description:
Filed is what filing Derived did, member by member as an assertion batch
reports it. Absent unless file was asked.

gained.description:
Gained is each that holds only without them — a negation those
assertions had been refuting. Empty when Without is absent.

lemmas.description:
Lemmas is every derived tuple of any other predicate a proof in Derived
cites, in the same order, so every support that is not an assertion can
be followed to a proof.

lost.description:
Lost is each tuple of the predicates asked for, asserted or derived, that
holds with everything and not without the assertions Without names.
Empty when Without is absent.

steps.description: Steps is the most rows one evaluation's joins examine.

truncated.description:
Truncated says a bound stopped the evaluation before its fixpoint. Every
tuple listed still holds; some that hold are missing.

entity.description:
Entity narrows the diff to what was asserted about one entity. Absent
diffs the whole graph, bounded by Limit.

from.description:
From is the earlier instant of the world, RFC 3339. What held here is
the baseline, so a statement beginning exactly at From is part of it and
not a change. Absent is To: the diff is then of what was heard, not of
what happened.

from_known.description:
FromKnown is how much this plane had heard at the baseline, RFC 3339.
Absent is ToKnown: the diff is then of the world, as known once.

limit.description:
Limit caps how many (entity, relation) pairs are examined, in key order.
Absent, zero, or anything above the walk ceiling is the ceiling.

to.description:
To is the later instant of the world, RFC 3339, and may not precede From.
A statement beginning or ending exactly at To is in the diff. Absent is
now.

to_known.description:
ToKnown is how much it had heard at the later point, RFC 3339, and may
not precede FromKnown. Absent is now.

asserted.description: Asserted is each statement holding at To that did not at From.

bound.description: Bound is how many pairs this diff examined at most.

from.description: From is the earlier instant, RFC 3339, echoed.

from_known.description: FromKnown is the knowledge instant of the baseline, RFC 3339.

retracted.description:
Retracted is each statement that held at From and no longer does at To,
with what ended it as Now: the retraction, the later value, or the
statement itself when its own until did.

superseded.description:
Superseded is each property whose value at From was replaced by a
different one at To, once per pair however many came in between.

to.description:
To is the later instant, RFC 3339: the one asked for, or the server's
clock when none was.

to_known.description: ToKnown is the knowledge instant of the later point, RFC 3339.

truncated.description:
Truncated says more pairs gathered assertions in the interval than Bound,
or that one pair holds more than a single read returns. Narrow by entity
or by a shorter interval to see the rest.

as_known.description:
AsKnown is how much this plane had heard, RFC 3339: the answer as it would
have been given then. Absent is now.

as_of.description:
AsOf is the instant of the world to answer about, RFC 3339: what held
then. Absent is now.

entity.description: Entity is the entity key to resolve. Required.

as_known.description: AsKnown is the knowledge instant this state was resolved at, RFC 3339.

as_of.description: AsOf is the valid instant this state was resolved at, RFC 3339.

entity.description: Entity is the folded entity key the question named.

expired.description:
Expired is every statement about the entity that was known by AsKnown and
begun by AsOf but no longer holds at AsOf because its until passed, a
retraction ended it, or a later statement superseded it.

incoming.description:
Incoming is every in-force edge pointing at the entity at the point,
ordered by source entity and relation key.

known.description:
Known is true when at least one property, outgoing edge, incoming edge or
expired statement was found for the entity.

outgoing.description:
Outgoing is every in-force edge asserted about the entity at the point,
ordered by relation key and then winner order.

properties.description:
Properties is every in-force scalar property of the entity at the point,
ordered by relation key.

scorecard.description:
Scorecard is the kinship and closeness scores holding on the entity,
highest score first.

truncated.description:
Truncated says the read of outgoing or incoming assertions hit the walk
ceiling.

type.description:
Type is the winning `type` of the entity at the point. Absent when no
type holds.

conflicts.description:
Conflicts is every weaker account of the winner's moment that names a
different value, strongest first.

contested.description: Contested is true exactly when Conflicts is not empty.

relation.description: Relation is the scalar relation's key.

value.description: Value is the winning scalar value holding at the point.

winner.description: Winner is the assertion that speaks for this relation at the point.

entity.description:
Entity is the key to erase. Every assertion ABOUT it and every edge
pointing AT it is removed, under every spelling it may have been filed
under — its NFC key, that key decomposed, and the bytes sent — so a subject
filed before keys were folded goes with the rest; a property whose scalar
happens to spell it is not a reference and stays. Required, 512 bytes at
most.

reason.description:
Reason is why, as the audit trail will keep it — a request number, a legal
basis. It outlives the erasure, so it may not contain the entity: refused
when it does. Required, 512 bytes at most.

at.description:
At is the instant of the erasure, RFC 3339, and the time on its audit
record.

by.description:
By is the identity that erased — `owner` or `owner/user` — from the
validated principal.

complete.description:
Complete is true only when no store may still hold the subject: every
store erased or absent and nothing Remaining. While a store is
unsupported it is false, and that store is handled out of band before
the erasure is done.

digest.description:
Digest is SHA-256, hex, over IDs in their ascending order, each written
`<length>:<id>` — the same content address an assertion's own ID is. The
audit trail records it in place of the ids, so the receipt verifies
against the trail and the trail names nothing.

entity.description:
Entity is the key that was erased, folded as every key here is (NFC, no
control characters) and echoed so a stored receipt says what it is for.
This plane keeps no copy of it.

ids.description: IDs are the content addresses of the assertions removed, ascending.

remaining.description:
Remaining is how many assertions still name the entity because one call
removes at most ten thousand. Non-zero means call again; each call is its
own receipt.

sources.description:
Sources are the documents the removed assertions were filed from. This
plane does not own them: ingesting one again files the subject again.

stores.description:
Stores is every store in this deployment that may hold what the org says
about the subject, and what happened in each: this graph first, then the
stores this op cannot reach.

refused.description:
Refused are the relations found that filing would refuse — a subject or
object whose type is not the relation's declared domain or range, or a
declaration from a caller who is not an admin — each carrying its reason.
Ingest records none of them.

triples.description:
Triples are the relations found that the caller may file, in the order
the document states them.

at.description:
At is when the thing was so, RFC 3339. Required, and refused when it sits
more than five minutes ahead of the server clock — an assertion dated
further out would never mature and would skew every read until it did.

confidence.description:
Confidence in [0,1]. A tie-breaker within the order, never a substitute
for it. Absent is 0, the weakest an assertion can be.

entity.description:
Entity is the thing being described, in the organization's own namespace.
It is not created: an entity exists because something was asserted about it.
It is a key, folded to Unicode NFC with control characters removed, so two
spellings of one name are one entity. An entity named `relation:<name>` is
that relation's declaration and one named `rule:<name>` is a rule
(graphDerive), and only an admin of the organization may assert anything
of either. Required, 512 bytes at most.

evidence.description:
Evidence points at the record this claim came from, 512 bytes at most. An
assertion without one is admitted and carries no defence.

names.description:
Names says the value is an entity. A walk reads only the edges, so this is
a declaration and never a guess about the value's shape.

relation.description:
Relation is what is being asserted — `depends`, `owner`, `same`, `title`
— and a key, folded as Entity is. It is open until the organization
declares it: once `relation:<name>` has a `domain` or `range` in force,
the entity's `type` (and, for range, the value's) must match it. Required,
128 bytes at most.

seen.description:
Seen is when this assertion became knowable, RFC 3339. Defaults to At and
may not precede it. It is provenance and it decides nothing: the instant
every read uses is derived as the later of Seen and the server's own clock.

source.description:
Source names who asserted. Required, because an assertion nobody is named
for cannot be weighed against one that is. Open text: this plane ranks no
source above another.

until.description:
Until is when the thing stopped being so, RFC 3339, and must follow At.
Absent is open: the statement holds until something ends it. A term of
office, an employment, a membership are At and Until on one statement.

value.description:
Value is what the relation points at. When Names is true it is another
entity's key, folded as Entity is, and the assertion is an EDGE; otherwise
it is a scalar, kept byte for byte, and the assertion is a property. 2048
bytes at most, or 512 when it names an entity.

assertions.description:
Assertions are the IDs of the assertions it cites, each a row a read of
this graph returns.

communities.description:
Communities are the communities of the facts it cites, at level 0 of the
partition at AsOf — the ids POST /v1/graph/communities answers with.

score.description: Score is how much the model judged it helps, 1 to 100.

text.description: Text is what the model found, in its words.

assertion.description: Assertion is the underlying scorecard assertion holding at the point.

relationship.description:
Relationship is the scorecard column, such as mother, father, partner,
family or familyAndFriends.

score.description: Score is the classifier probability in [0,1].

as_known.description:
AsKnown is how much this plane had heard, RFC 3339: the answer as it would
have been given then, which is what makes a past answer reproducible.
Absent is now.

as_of.description:
AsOf walks the graph as it stood at an instant of the world, RFC 3339:
the edges that held then. Absent is now.

depth.description: Depth is how many hops. Absent is one.

direction.description:
Direction is out, in or both. Out follows an edge from its entity to its
value — what the node points at; in follows it the other way — what points
at the node; both is the union of the two, not a third rule. Absent is out.

relation.description:
Relation narrows the walk to one edge relation. Absent follows all. Only
edges IN FORCE are ever followed — the assertion that wins its (entity,
relation) at the instant — so a superseded or retracted edge is not a hop,
and neither is a property.

seeds.description: Seeds is where the walk starts. At least one.

bound.description:
Bound is the ceiling this walk was held to, the same for every caller, so
Truncated can be read against a number rather than guessed at.

depth.description:
Depth is the deepest hop count actually reached. It is at most the depth
asked for, and smaller when the walk ran out of edges first.

entities.description:
Entities is everything reached, the seeds included, ordered by the fewest
hops that reach each one and then by key.

truncated.description:
Truncated says the bound stopped the walk. The bound is part of the answer
rather than a silent short read.

edge.description:
Edge is true for the relationship-type classes (CS* and nm_*RelationshipType)
that reify a two-row edge sharing a relationshipId in stable_graph.

group.description:
Group is the class family: core, person, attribute, place, event,
activity, activity type, transport, media, animal, commerce or edge.

id.description: ID is the raw code stored in graph.db, such as SB104, CS165 or nm_walletOrder.

label.description:
Label is the human-readable class name, such as person or employment
relationship type.

mechanism.description:
Mechanism records whether the daemon mechanism populating the class is
implemented, unverified or unlocated.

group.description:
Group is the feature block: identity (0..19), communication (20..59) or
photos (60..143).

index.description: Index is the feature's 0-based position (0..143) in metadata.json.

name.description:
Name is Apple's feature identifier, such as sameLastName or
photosPersonPosteriorProbabilityGivenSaturdayNight.

classes.description: Classes is the matching entity classes (181 in the unfiltered catalog).

features.description:
Features is the matching EntityTagging classifier features (144 in the
unfiltered catalog).

predicates.description: Predicates is the matching predicates (278 in the unfiltered catalog).

score_columns.description:
ScoreColumns is the 17 relationship columns of entityTagging.db's
kinship scorecard.

id.description:
ID is the raw predicate code stored in graph.db, such as PS1, PS500 or
nm_isCurrentUser.

label.description: Label is the plain-language reading of what the predicate records.

mechanism.description:
Mechanism records whether the daemon mechanism is implemented, unverified
or unlocated.

method.description:
Method names how the daemon obtains the value: Copied, Joined, Rule,
Apple-shipped, Embedding model, XGBoost, Face clustering or Local LLM.

names.description:
Names is true when the predicate links its subject to another entity
rather than a scalar literal.

relation.description:
Relation is the canonical snake_case relation key this plane files the
predicate under when ingesting an Apple graph.

source.description: Source names the OS store or subsystem the daemon reads the predicate from.

as_known.description:
AsKnown is how much this plane had heard, RFC 3339: the answer as it would
have been given then, which is what makes a past answer reproducible.
Absent is now.

as_of.description:
AsOf finds the path through the graph as it stood at an instant of the
world, RFC 3339: an edge that did not hold then is not crossed. Absent is
now.

direction.description:
Direction is out, in or both. Out crosses each edge from its entity to
its value; in crosses it backwards; both crosses it either way. Absent is
out.

from.description: From is the entity the path starts at. Required.

relations.description:
Relations is the edge relations a path may cross. Absent crosses every
relation. A causal chain is this list naming the relations that mean
cause — `caused_by` and `influenced` under the decision convention. At
most 256.

to.description: To is the entity the path ends at. Required.

as_known.description: AsKnown is the knowledge instant it was taken at, RFC 3339, the same way.

as_of.description:
AsOf is the instant the path was taken at, RFC 3339: the one asked for,
or the server's clock when none was.

bound.description: Bound is the ceiling the search was held to, the same one a walk is.

decay.description:
Decay is the product of the edges' confidences: how much certainty
survives the whole chain. Absent unless every edge states a confidence
above zero — an unstated confidence reads as zero, and a product of
numbers nobody gave measures nothing.

edges.description:
Edges is the path from From to To, one assertion per hop, each with its
source, evidence and filer. An edge is listed as it was asserted, so
under in or both it may point against the direction of travel.

found.description:
Found is false when no path of in-force edges joins the two within the
bound. That is an answer, not an error.

hops.description:
Hops is how many edges the path crosses: zero when From is To, and zero
when nothing was found.

truncated.description:
Truncated says the bound stopped the search before a path was found, so
Found false means none within the bound rather than none at all.

weakest.description:
Weakest is the edge with the lowest confidence, the first of them on a
tie: the link the chain is only as strong as. Absent exactly when Decay
is.

assertions.description:
Assertions are the matching rows: a read's in the order they were written,
oldest first; a search's best match first. Every version is here: this
resolves nothing and withholds nothing, so a superseded claim and the one
that superseded it both appear.

as_known.description:
AsKnown is how much this plane had heard, RFC 3339: the answer as it would
have been given then, which is what makes a past answer reproducible.
Absent is now.

as_of.description:
AsOf is the instant of the world to answer about, RFC 3339: what held
then. Absent is now.

entity.description: Entity is the thing to answer about. Required.

relation.description:
Relation is the one relation to settle. Required: this answers a single
(entity, relation) pair, never a whole entity at once.

as_known.description: AsKnown is the knowledge instant it was taken at, RFC 3339, the same way.

as_of.description:
AsOf is the valid instant this answer was taken at, RFC 3339: the one
asked for, or the server's clock when none was.

conflicts.description:
Conflicts is, for a relation holding one value, every weaker account of
the winner's moment that names a different value, strongest first. They
lost the order and stay visible, so a disagreement is never resolved into
silence.

contested.description: Contested is true exactly when Conflicts is not empty.

entity.description:
Entity is the entity the question named, echoed so a stored answer still
says what it is about.

held.description:
Held is every statement holding at the point, Winner first, one per
value: one for a relation that holds one value at a time, and every one
the pair holds for a relation that holds many — the five holders of a
position over five terms are five.

known.description:
Known is false when nothing held at the point. That is an answer, not an
error.

relation.description: Relation is the relation the question named, echoed for the same reason.

truncated.description:
Truncated says this pair holds more statements than one read returns, so
the answer was decided from the ceiling-full begun most recently. It is
reported because a provenance plane that trims silently is a plane that
answers confidently and wrongly; narrow the question with as_of to see
what it dropped.

winner.description:
Winner is the statement holding at the point that began most recently,
then the strongest under the order `rule` names. Absent exactly when Known
is false.

at.description:
At is when what the source says was so, RFC 3339. Required by ingest — which
records — and read by nothing in extract, which records nothing. Required for
the same reason /v1/graph requires it: it is part of the assertion's content
address, so re-reading one source at one instant records one set of rows
however many times it is delivered. A clock read here instead would append
the whole document again on every re-read.

source.description:
Source names where the text came from — a URL, a document id, a page title.
It is stamped on every assertion as its source, and with the section number
as its evidence, so a claim can be traced back to the passage that made it.
Required.

subject.description:
Subject is the entity the text is about before any heading names one. A
document that states relations above its first heading needs it; one whose
every section is headed does not.

text.description:
Text is the document. Relations are read from it and from nothing else: a
line written `relation:: value` states one, and prose states none. Required.

detail.description:
Detail says what an unsupported store is missing before an erasure could
reach it.

removed.description: Removed is how many of its rows were removed.

status.description:
Status is erased (rows naming the entity were removed), absent (it held
none) or unsupported (this op cannot reach it, so it may still hold the
subject).

store.description:
Store names it: `graph` is the caller's own (org, project) assertion
file, its full-text index included; `knowledge` is the org's wiki pages,
memories and sources with their vectors; `ai.memory` is /v1/ai/memory.

assertion.description:
Assertion is the ID of the statement in force the atom rests on. Absent
when the atom is itself derived: it is then an entry of Derived or
Lemmas, with a proof of its own.

object.description:
Object is its second argument. Absent for a predicate the rules use with
one argument.

predicate.description: Predicate is the relation the supporting atom is of.

names.description:
Names is the author's declaration that Object is an entity and the assertion
is an EDGE, written `[[key]]`. Absent, the relation is a property of Subject.
It is read from the notation and never guessed from the value's shape.

object.description:
Object is what the relation points at. When Names is true it has been
unwrapped from its `[[…]]` and is another entity's key.

predicate.description:
Predicate is the relation, exactly as the line spells it before the `::`.
This surface holds no vocabulary, so it renames nothing.

reason.description:
Reason is why filing it would be refused: the declared schema, or a
declaration from a caller who is not an admin of the organization. Present
only on a member of Refused.

section.description:
Section is which section of the source stated it, counting from zero. It is
the second half of every resulting assertion's evidence, `<source>#<section>`.

subject.description:
Subject is the entity the statement is about: the nearest heading above the
line, or the request's own subject where no heading has appeared yet.

at.description:
At is when this turn was spoken, RFC 3339. Absent defaults to the
conversation's At instant.

id.description:
ID is the turn's identifier within the conversation, appended to Source
as `#<id>` in Evidence. Absent defaults to its 1-based position.

partner.description:
Partner is the entity key of the participant addressed in this turn.
Second-person references (you, your) resolve to Partner.

speaker.description:
Speaker is the entity key of the participant speaking this turn. First-
person references (I, me, my) resolve to Speaker. Required.

text.description: Text is what the speaker said. Required.

bound.description: Bound is the ceiling on one walk.

relations.description:
Relations is what this organization has actually asserted. This plane
declares none of its own.

rule.description:
Rule names the terms of the precedence order, in the order they apply. A
reader who is told a winner without the rule cannot check it.

schema.description:
Schema is what the organization has declared, in force now: each relation
with a domain or range, asserted as (`relation:<name>`, `domain` |
`range`, `<type>`) and checked against the entities' (`<entity>`, `type`,
`<type>`). A relation absent here is open.

A decision is an entity of type `decision` by convention, never enforced:
`scenario`, `reasoning`, `outcome` and `confidence` are its properties;
`decided_by`, `caused_by`, `influenced` and `precedent` are its edges.
Declare their domain and range to make that convention checked; find a
precedent with search, then neighbors over `precedent`.

at.description: At is when the thing was so, RFC 3339, as the asserter gave it.

by.description:
By is the identity that filed it — `owner` or `owner/user` — stamped from
the validated principal at the write, never from the body.

confidence.description:
Confidence in [0,1] as the asserter gave it; absent is 0. It breaks a tie
between two assertions equally knowable and decides nothing else.

entity.description: Entity is the thing described, in the organization's own namespace.

evidence.description:
Evidence points at the record the claim came from. Absent when the asserter
gave none.

id.description:
ID is the assertion's content address, minted by the server from what was
asserted. Two callers who assert the identical thing land on one ID and one
row; changing any asserted field makes a different ID and a second row.

knowable.description:
Knowable is the first instant this plane could have answered with the
assertion, RFC 3339: the later of Seen and the server's clock at the write.
Derived and never supplied, which is what stops history filed today from
being backdated into a past read.

names.description:
Names true means the assertion is an edge and Value is an entity. A walk
reads only these.

relation.description: Relation is what was asserted of it.

seen.description:
Seen is when the asserter says it became knowable, RFC 3339. Provenance
only — Knowable is what an as-of read is bounded by.

source.description:
Source names who asserted, as the caller gave it. This plane ranks no
source above another, so it never outweighs a later Knowable.

until.description:
Until is when the thing stopped being so, RFC 3339, as the asserter gave
it. Absent is open.

value.description:
Value is what the relation points at: another entity's key when Names is
true, otherwise a scalar.

code.description: A stable token a client can branch on, when the refusal names one.

detail.description: What was refused, for a person to read.

bearer.description: The caller's credential, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. It is either an access token minted by Hanzo IAM or an API key (pk-/sk-). X-Authorization, and HTTP Basic carrying the token as the password, are accepted spellings of the same header for clients that cannot set Authorization; a browser presents the session cookie instead. Every operation requires it unless it says `security: []`.
